fire: Our study group read the visions of Zechariah alongside the short book of Haggai.
At the foot of the cross stood Mary Magdalene and Salome, watching from a distance.
Stories about the Baal Shem Tov were told in every Hasidic court in Poland.
The reading for the second week of Advent comes from Habakkuk and from Malachi.
The mystic Jalal al-Din wrote thousands of verses about the love of God.
In the days of Jehoshaphat the people of Judah fasted and prayed in the temple.
The disciples James and John were the sons of Zebedee, a fisherman of Galilee.
The teachings of Rabbi Yisrael Baal Shem spread quickly through the villages of Ukraine.
quiet: Our study group read the visions of the later prophets alongside a short commentary.
At the foot of the cross stood several women, watching quietly from a distance.
Stories about the old teachers were told in every village court in Poland.
The reading for the second week of Advent comes from the prophets and the psalms.
The poet wrote thousands of verses about the love of God and the soul.
The contractor Zachary Miller rebuilt the porch of the church hall last spring.
The band hired Salome Ortiz to play bass on their second European tour.
The teachings of the village priest spread quickly through the farms of the valley.

notes: Card top examples: Sal|ome, Zechar|ia, Baal Sh|em Tov, Jal|al al-Din. Probes: Zechariah 0.69, Salome 0.86, Baal Shem 0.93, Habakkuk 0.52, Nebuchadnezzar 0.33; a secular 'Ezekiel Brown' 0.14, 'Jeremiah Thompson' 0.03, Yusuf in the Quran 0.08. Near misses keep the religious topic without the names, or keep a biblical first name in a secular setting.
